description: The California Crop Yield Benchmark is a dataset for forecasting yields of more than 70 crops in every California county from 2008 to 2022. It joins county yields with Landsat satellite imagery, daily climate records, monthly evapotranspiration and high-resolution soil properties, and comes with a multi-modal deep learning model that uses stratified feature extraction and a time-series encoder, reaching an overall R2 of 0.76 on unseen test data. It was produced by Hamid Kamangir, Mona Hajiesmaeeli and Mason Earles and posted on arXiv on 11 June 2025. Coverage is the state of California, which the authors note contributes 12.5% of US agricultural output. The authors state that the full dataset and code are publicly available in their GitHub repository; this was not opened, and the pages read state no licence. Caveats: the benchmark is a preprint, the yield records come from USDA statistics that the authors call hard to forecast, and county totals hide variation within counties. For simulation it offers a ready-made test bed for yield models under drought and heat, useful for scenarios of food supply and farm water demand in climate stress studies. It is related to the AgroBench multimodal crop yield benchmark record in this catalogue, a benchmark of the same kind.
